text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Key member of Socialist Edek party accuses Communist Akel of interfering with internal affairs of the party and poaching its supporters.
- Turkish reconaissance planes were detected on army radars over Paphos and Limassol last week.

- Britain prepares for an intensive round of contacts in May and June aimed at achieving an agreement between Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash on a solution to the Cyprus problem.
- The United Nations and the United States see any improvement in Turkey-European Union relations as the key to any progress towards achieving a solution on Cyprus.
- Interior Ministry proposes that all nationals of EU countries have free entry to Cyprus.
- Socialist Edek party leader Vasos Lyssarides tells a party conference: "I will never be a satellite of any party."
- Greece is expected to fight at the EU Council of Ministers meeting today for the exclusion of Turkish Cypriots from accession negotiations with Europe.
- Tourist bookings to Cyprus have fallen by 20 percent over last year.
